clue.text: In general, an occasion that would be familiar to musicians

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for a noun: the definition describes the thing rather than naming it

parts.note: general in the sense of shared by all, widespread
an occasion, as in 'that time we met'

explanation.surface: A gig or performance that any working musician would recognise as routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Common time is 4/4, the commonest musical metre, marked with a C on the stave. The definition is loose: it describes the answer as something musicians know.
explanation.definitionFit: Common time, four crotchet beats to the bar, is basic notation every trained musician meets early.

clue.text: Miner's tailless dog

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter, the tail of the word, is cut off

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: A miner owns a dog with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive suggests the dog belongs to the miner; really the miner's word loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a sheepdog breed from Scotland and northern England.

clue.text: I object to publicity for drink

parts.note: me is the object form of I
an ad, an advertisement, is publicity

explanation.surface: Someone protests against advertising alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' reads as a protest; grammatically, the object case of I is me.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic beverage made by fermenting honey with water.

clue.text: State show'?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical

explanation.walkthrough: 'State show' sounds like an official exhibition or a state occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a US state and to a 1943 Broadway musical, the stage show Oklahoma!

clue.text: Novelist uses letters from Dr Worth to Lenin

indicators.note: using the letters from some words means taking all of them and building something new

parts.note: every letter of these four words

explanation.surface: A novelist borrows passages from a doctor's correspondence with Lenin.
explanation.definitionFit: Thornton Wilder was an American novelist and playwright, author of The Bridge of San Luis Rey.

clue.text: In man upset the islander

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside another, wrapped by it

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the following word is read from the bottom upwards, against the usual direction

parts.note: the word split as up and set: set is taken as written, and up is the signal to turn it

explanation.surface: Someone from an island is thrown into turmoil by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as one word meaning distressed; split as up and set, it reverses set in this down light, and the result goes inside the man.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maltese is a native of Malta, the Mediterranean island nation south of Sicily.

clue.text: Note to redhead found by emperor in cave

parts.note: G is one of the musical notes A to G
the head, or first letter, of red
Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors

explanation.surface: Someone passes a message to a red-haired person, discovered with an emperor hiding in a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' reads as a red-haired person but means the first letter of red.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave, often natural or artificial in a garden.

clue.text: Are mobilised by the. German admiral

indicators.note: mobilised troops are moved about, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
der is German for the

explanation.surface: Forces are called up by a German admiral.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop is a printing slip. Erich Raeder commanded the German navy from 1928 to 1943.
explanation.definitionFit: Raeder was a grand admiral, head of the German navy before Dönitz.

clue.text: Work of fiction might appear freshest to a gay type

indicators.note: what might appear from some letters is something they could be reshaped into

parts.note: all the letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A novel might strike a cheerful sort of person as the freshest thing around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' gives no letters and only rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forsyte Saga is John Galsworthy's sequence of novels about a wealthy London family.

clue.text: College full of spirited scholars?

parts.note: surface reading: a college whose students are lively and energetic; setter's reading: every member is a soul, a spirit, so the college is named for all of them

explanation.walkthrough: All Souls is an Oxford college with no undergraduates, only elected fellows; 'spirited' plays on souls as spirits of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: All Souls College, Oxford, is a real college, famous for its demanding fellowship exam.

clue.text: Disclosed way to get round woman with drink

indicators.note: to get round something is to surround it, so the first piece encloses the others

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
Eve, the first woman
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A route by which someone circles round a woman holding a drink, now made public.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose something is to reveal it, so the two past participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Composer is to deal with sound

indicators.note: with sound means the words are taken by how they are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to handle something is to deal with it

explanation.surface: A composer has to cope with the acoustics, or with the music itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal with' reads as one verb phrase; 'with' also starts the sound indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was the German-born Baroque composer of Messiah.

clue.text: Enthusiasts confuse Dove with another river

indicators.note: to confuse is to mix up, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the Dove, an English river, taken as written
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Keen fans mistake the River Dove for some other river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dove and the Tees are both rivers in England; capitalised Dove pretends to be the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotees are ardent followers or fans of something, the same as enthusiasts.

clue.text: Wind is from the west — or might be

indicators.note: is from says the answer is taken straight out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the words west, or and might

explanation.surface: A forecaster says the wind is westerly, or perhaps it could be.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a hedging weather report; the 'or might be' joke is that a westerly gale may indeed be one.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm is a very strong wind, a gale-force blow.

clue.text: Novel form of moon-jets

indicators.note: a new form of something is the same material reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of moon-jets, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A new type of lunar jet propulsion, as if from science fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; it is the definition, a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Jones is Henry Fielding's 1749 comic novel about a foundling.

clue.text: Three articles found under the counter are of this fabric

indicators.note: in a down clue, found under means placed below, so these pieces follow

parts.note: a bar is the counter in a pub
a, the and a: indefinite, definite, indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Goods sold illicitly under the counter are made of this cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the counter' reads as the idiom for illicit trade, but here it places the articles beneath a bar in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine woollen fabric with a lightly ribbed weave, used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Scope given to fine old actor

parts.note: play as in room to move, freedom of movement
fine weather is fair weather

explanation.surface: An elderly actor is given plenty of freedom to do as he likes.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Nigel Playfair (1874-1934) was an English actor-manager who ran the Lyric, Hammersmith.
explanation.definitionFit: Playfair was a stage performer of the early twentieth century, so an actor from the past.

clue.text: Settled real contents of a letter

parts.note: a bird that has lit on a branch has settled

indicators.note: contents are what fills something in any order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Settling what a letter really said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents' is an unusual signal to rearrange and may be a misprint. 'Real' also hints at the answer's commonest sense, actual or exact.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal comes from Latin littera, a letter, and means relating to letters of the alphabet.

clue.text: Letter written by old actor demanding food

parts.note: en is the name of the letter N
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree, Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A note from a veteran actor insisting on being fed.
explanation.walkthrough: Beerbohm Tree (1852-1917) founded RADA and ran His Majesty's Theatre in London.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrée is a dish served at a meal, a main course in America or before the main in Britain.

clue.text: Omit charges for errands

parts.note: to miss something out is to omit it
ions are electrically charged particles

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave fees off the bill for running errands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' reads as fees; it means charged particles.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission is a task someone is sent out to do, which is what an errand is.

clue.text: Contemptible complaint?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the disease caused by lack of vitamin C

explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grumble; it means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means despicable, and the noun is a deficiency illness, a medical complaint sailors once suffered.

clue.text: In new hat, girl appears a goddess

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so these letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
Ena is a girl's name, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A girl in a new hat looks like a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only sets the scene; the rearranged hat comes first and the girl's name follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena is the Greek goddess of wisdom and war, patron of Athens.

clue.text: Perhaps upsets one sort of beginners?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ship that capsizes and sinks ...
second meaning: people who found or start an institution

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads loosely: to founder is to fill and sink, as an upset boat does. The second is the noun, those who found something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for sinking or collapsing and a plural noun for people who establish things.

clue.text: Worry about entering short measure

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: FT is the short form of foot, a measure
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Fretting over being served less than a full measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short measure' reads as being cheated at the bar; it means an abbreviated unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious and worry continually.

clue.text: Gill, for example, could be given a rest

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gill is an organ a fish breathes with
second meaning: a short pause to recover

explanation.walkthrough: Gill reads as a woman's name, someone who deserves a break; it is the fish's breathing organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing organ is literally a thing that breathes, and a pause to get one's breath back is the everyday sense.

clue.text: Knave of a servant? That's about right

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a valet is a manservant
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a rogue is one of the servants, and is told that's roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's about right' reads as agreement; 'about' is working as a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Varlet is an archaic word for a rascal or rogue, originally a page or attendant.

clue.text: Excuses an attempt' to make a joke

parts.note: pleas offered in mitigation are excuses
taken as written
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for an attempt at humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a light humorous remark, a little joke in conversation.
